messages:
rachel-peopleops: Quick benefits Q  - If an employee has an outstanding 401(k) loan and goes on unpaid leave for 12 weeks, what happens to payroll loan repayments? Do they get paused, accrue interest, or go into default? Trying to give clear guidance.
ethan-eng: Good one. I had to go unpaid for a week once and payroll just paused deductions; loan stayed open and interest accrued. But if payroll misses too many payments the loan can be treated as a distribution. Vendor rules vary.
tara-finance: Correct  - recordkeeper policy matters. Typically: deductions stop if there's no payroll, interest keeps accruing, and if repayments stop long enough the outstanding balance may be deemed a taxable distribution. We should share vendor-specific thresholds.
rachel-peopleops: Do we offer any company-level protections or temporary forbearance options?
benefits@redwood: Our recordkeeper offers a short-term suspension option in some cases (medical/FMLA) but it must be requested before loan hits default status. They require a form and sponsor approval. For leaves >90 days we often coordinate a formal forbearance. Manual interest capitalization rules apply per plan doc.
payroll-bot: FYI: payroll cannot process loan payments when earnings are $0. If you want to keep paying, submit an ACH form to the recordkeeper or set up an after-tax catch-up via payroll hold request prior to leave. Link: https://payroll.redwood.com/forms/loan-ACH
tara-finance: Action items: 1) employee discusses with manager/HR; 2) benefits@redwood opens case with recordkeeper to request suspension or forbearance; 3) if employee wants to continue repayments while unpaid, they must complete ACH form before last paycheck.
ethan-eng: What's the tax consequence if loan is treated as distribution? Does it count as W-2 income?
tara-finance: If deemed distribution, it's treated as taxable income and if under 59.5 may be subject to 10% early withdrawal penalty. It will be reported on Form 1099-R. Finance can run scenarios for gross-up if needed but that's rare.
rachel-peopleops: Good notes. I'll add a short FAQ and checklist to the benefits portal: "401(k) loans and unpaid leave" with the steps and links. benefits@redwood can we get the recordkeeper form/template to attach?
benefits@redwood: Will attach the forbearance request, ACH form, and vendor FAQ to the portal today and open a vendor case for common timelines. Case# RK-2026-1123.
tara-finance: Also recommend managers remind folks to pause or redirect pre-tax deferrals before leave if they plan to stop contributions.
rachel-peopleops: Thanks team  :thumbsup:
